localBiteReport: This week's most current report (week of October 23–29, 2026) comes from Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters, who covers Choctawhatchee Bay for the Great Days Outdoors Northwest Florida Fishing Report. Despite a recent hurricane, the bay stayed relatively clear with only a tannin-stained tint, and the redfish bite on the flats has held up well — smaller slot fish (roughly 23 inches and under) are still working familiar guts, potholes, and shallow feeding areas, while larger upper-slot and overslot reds are shifting into a more mobile fall pattern. Water temp at this location is 77°F, consistent with the recent cold fronts that are nudging fish toward more aggressive fall feeding. A guide report on captainexperiences.com from approximately two weeks ago noted that redfish and trout were heating up in the bayous, which aligns with the current picture. Sheepshead are expected to pick up in coming weeks according to a Santa Rosa Beach captain on the same platform, but have not been prominently featured in this week's bay reports.
